recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中央偏左一顆含橘紅色粗顆粒的嗜酸性球，胞質內吞入一團圓形、均質、淡紫色的核物質，把自己的細胞核推到邊緣；這是發生在嗜酸性球的 LE 細胞現象。
features: Eosinophil with coarse orange-red specific granules and its nucleus displaced to the periphery
Large, round, smooth, homogeneous pale lilac intracytoplasmic inclusion lacking chromatin pattern (phagocytosed denatured nuclear material)
Surrounding cellular aspirate with myelocytes, band and segmented neutrophils, erythroid precursors and lymphocytes
Clean background with scattered platelets and cell debris
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear is cellular with maturing myeloid and erythroid elements. Near the center, an eosinophil with coarse orange-red granules contains a large, round, homogeneous lilac intracytoplasmic body that displaces the eosinophil nucleus to the periphery; the inclusion lacks a recognizable chromatin pattern, consistent with phagocytosed denatured nuclear material. The same phenomenon in neutrophils defines the classic LE cell. Findings are consistent with an LE-cell phenomenon involving an eosinophil in the setting of systemic lupus erythematosus.

ddx.vs: The engulfed nucleus in a tart cell retains visible chromatin structure and the host is usually a monocyte/macrophage, whereas the LE body is smooth and homogeneous.
Ingested apoptotic cells show dense pyknotic chromatin fragments or a recognizable cell outline rather than a single swollen, structureless lilac mass.

ddx.dx: Dysplastic eosinophil with separated nuclear lobes
ddx.vs: Nuclear lobes stain dark with coarse chromatin and remain connected by filaments, unlike the pale, structureless ingested LE body.
